questions.q: A cheerful pop song keeps playing on a radio while a character is tortured. What does Chion call this, and what does it usually do?
choices: Empathetic music; it tells us to feel sad
Mickey-Mousing; it makes the scene comic
Anempathetic music; its indifference sharpens our horror
A leitmotif; it identifies the villain
questions.explain: Anempathetic music carries on regardless of the scene, and the world's indifference intensifies our response.

questions.q: A composer writes a trombone slide for every pratfall and a pizzicato note for each tiptoe in a serious drama. What's the likely criticism?
choices: It's Mickey-Mousing, and in drama it usually feels cartoonish
It's anempathetic and too cold
It's a needle drop and the lyrics compete with dialogue
It's a leitmotif that never develops
questions.explain: Music that imitates action note for note is named after early Disney cartoons.

questions.q: A short theme plays whenever the heroine's lost brother is mentioned, and returns softly at the end when she remembers him. What's the technique?
choices: A needle drop
A leitmotif
Room tone
A drop-out
questions.explain: A leitmotif ties a musical idea to a character or idea and lets music carry memory.

questions.q: What did Hitchcock originally want for the Psycho shower murder?
choices: A jazz score
A Bernard Herrmann love theme
No music at all
A pop song on the radio
questions.explain: Hitchcock wanted silence; Herrmann wrote the shrieking strings anyway, and Hitchcock changed his mind.

questions.q: Claudia Gorbman's Unheard Melodies argues that the classical Hollywood score...
choices: Should always be diegetic
Works best when we don't consciously notice it, which also makes it quietly manipulative
Was invented by John Williams
Should copy the action note for note
questions.explain: Gorbman describes music that shapes our feeling below the level of attention.

questions.q: A writer has a big emotional reveal and plans a swelling string cue under it. A script editor says, "Try it with nothing." What's the reasoning?
choices: Silence against an expected cue makes us lean in, and lets the moment land without being told how to feel
Silence is always better than music
Music is only allowed if it's diegetic
Strings are a leitmotif and must be saved for the villain
questions.explain: Withholding music can be more powerful than an empathetic cue that over-tells.

questions.q: Why might a filmmaker choose an existing song (a needle drop) over composed score?
choices: Because songs can't be anempathetic
Because songs never compete with dialogue
Because the law requires it for montages
Because a song brings its own era, lyrics and associations into the scene
questions.explain: That's the shortcut, and the trap: the song's baggage comes with it.

ideas: Music that carries on cheerfully while something terrible happens can make the scene more disturbing, not less.
The best-behaved film score is one the audience never consciously hears.
A recurring theme tied to a character lets the music carry memory and change as the story does.
Music that copies the action beat for beat turns drama into a cartoon.
